transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-02-14
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ravi (CTO), Asha (Head of Platform), Ben (SRE), Nadia (Data Eng)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): kickoff/check-in for onboarding private/dedicated deployment for inference. discussed network, sizing, security, bench plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentine's day, we'll try to be quick. I'm Maya from Redwood, joined by Diego our SE and Priya from success. How are folks?
[00:06] Ravi Patel: Good, thanks. Lots to cover, appreciate you fitting this in.
[00:10] Asha Kaur: Hi all, yep we got the agenda, main things for us are networking and understanding the Dedicated sizing.
[00:16] Diego Alvarez: Great. Quick intro from our side: Diego, I own benchmarks and runtime tuning; we've seen customers in logistics use 95th percentile latency targets around 200-400ms for route prediction workloads.
[00:26] Ben Lowe: That sounds about right, our SLAs internally are 500ms p95 for external-facing services but for internal routing we'd like sub-300 ideally.
[00:32] Maya Chen: Perfect, goal of this sync is to align on pilot scope: Private control plane + Dedicated GPU pools, network setup (VPC peering vs site-to-site VPN), security controls (KMS, audit logs), and staffing handoffs. We'll recap next steps at the end.
[00:44] Nadia Ortiz: Quick note, our payloads are fairly large—embedding + context, typical request ~1.2k tokens. Hope that affects the sizing calc.
[00:52] Diego Alvarez: Good call. That sequence length matters a lot, it changes KV cache and memory pressure. For 1.2k average we'll likely recommend a mixed quant profile. We'll show numbers in the sizing worksheet.
[01:04] Asha Kaur: Can you explain what you mean by mixed quant profile? We had an internal infra doc that said quantization might drop accuracy and we want to avoid regressions.
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: Yeah totally. Mixed quant means we quantize some layers to int8 while keeping critical attention layers in higher precision. It reduces mem and inference cost but preserves quality. We also run evals on your prompt set to confirm no regression.
[01:23] Ravi Patel: How do you validate quality? We need a reproducible evaluation so our product folks sign off.
[01:29] Priya Rao: We usually take a representative prompt set—customer provides 200-500 prompts—run baseline on their current model, then on suggested quantized variant and compare metrics: BLEU-ish for structured outputs or custom scoring you provide. We can keep this in a shared spreadsheet.
[01:41] Ben Lowe: Ok, we'll pull a set.
[01:43] Asha Kaur: On network: we're leaning to VPC peering inside our cloud region because we want low latency and avoid NAT egress costs. But security wants an audit of peering endpoints. Is that standard?
[01:54] Diego Alvarez: Both options are common. VPC peering gives lower latency but requires CIDR planning; site-to-site VPN works if peering isn't approved. For private deployments we support both; for Dedicated capacity in our hosted racks we can also do dedicated interconnect if that's an option for you.
[02:07] Maya Chen: If I may add—some customers prefer a hybrid: peering for production traffic and VPN for admin access. We'll send a network checklist.
[02:15] Asha Kaur: That would help. Also, firewall rules—egress to Redwood control plane endpoints.
[02:19] Maya Chen: We'll include a minimal egress rule list and the control plane hostnames/IPs.
[02:25] [02:25] Ravi Patel: On the Dedicated sizing, can you walk through how you size GPU pools? We saw a note about continuous batching; how does that impact latency?
[02:33] Diego Alvarez: Sure. We model request qps, sequence length distribution, and concurrency. Continuous batching lets us lower per-token cost by grouping concurrent requests but it can add a small wait (tens of ms) if qps is low. For Westlane, if you expect bursts (peak routing times), autoscaling plus burst capacity will keep p95 within target. We'll provide baseline numbers in the worksheet, e.g., for 10k req/day with 1.2k tokens average and 400 concurrent users, we'd estimate X GPUs — exact numbers to follow.
[02:55] Ben Lowe: What's X? give ballpark, we need to budget.
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: Ballpark: for that profile maybe 2-4 A10x or equivalent for dedicated pools depending on quant and batching windows. But again we'll send a detailed table.
[03:09] Nadia Ortiz: Our data retention policy requires no request payloads be stored beyond 7 days and all logs be hashed. Can Redwood support that?
[03:17] Maya Chen: Yes—Private deployments let you control data plane, and our logging has configurable retention; we can set 7 days. For hosted or Dedicated, we have options to disable payload retention and store only audit hashes. We'll also document KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
[03:30] Asha Kaur: SOC2 and ISO — do you have certs? We need to add that to our vendor list.
[03:35] Priya Rao: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and are in process for ISO 27001; I can drop the compliance pack. Also we'll share the audit log export format.
[03:43] Ravi Patel: Great. About runbook and oncall: we want a handoff doc and clear escalation path. Who do we contact 24/7 if a model blows up in prod?
[03:52] Maya Chen: For Dedicated customers we include a support SLA and a shared oncall rota with an on-call SE. Priya will draft the runbook and propose a rotation.
[03:59] Priya Rao: We'll include contact channels (PagerDuty, Slack) and an incident playbook—for common issues like KV cache evictions, OOM, and model regressions.
[04:09] Ben Lowe: Do you have automated alerts for latency SLO breaches?
[04:13] Diego Alvarez: Yes, our dashboard emits alerts at thresholds (p50/p95/p99) and we can wire those to your PagerDuty. We also suggest synthetic checks.
[04:20] Asha Kaur: Benchmark plan—what does a pilot look like? We want to validate p95 latency and accuracy over a 2-week window.
[04:28] Diego Alvarez: Typical pilot: run an initial baseline (day 0) against your current infra, then we deploy Redwood Private + Dedicated in a staging VPC, run controlled load tests (hourly profiles) and continuous sampling of real traffic via shadowing for 2 weeks. Metrics we'll capture: token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per token, and quality regressions per prompt set. At the end, we review and decide go/no-go.
[04:48] Nadia Ortiz: Shadowing real traffic—does that require modifying our routing? We prefer minimal code changes.
[04:53] Diego Alvarez: Usually a lightweight proxy or sidecar that duplicates requests to Redwood for async evaluation works. We can provide a simple lambda or k8s sidecar sample.
[04:59] Ravi Patel: Ok, can you outline the schedule? We want to start pilot in two weeks.
[05:04] Maya Chen: Timeline proposal: Customer shares network details this week, we propose sizing & pricing by 2028-02-18, SE provides test harness by 2028-02-20, pilot window 2028-02-27 to 2028-03-12, with daily 15-minute standups in the first 3 days, then every other day checks. Does that work?
[05:20] Asha Kaur: That works for our infra folks, I'll confirm with security on peering.
[05:24] Ben Lowe: One question about audit logs: are they immutable? We need tamper evidence.
[05:29] Priya Rao: Our audit logs are append-only with integrity checks; for Private deployments you can route logs to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk) using our forwarder.
[05:37] Ravi Patel: Pricing: what are the main levers? We need an estimated monthly commit cost.
[05:41] Maya Chen: Main levers: number/type of GPUs reserved (Dedicated), quantization profile, batching windows, and cache hit rate. We'll send a worksheet with scenarios: conservative (no quant, higher perf), balanced (mixed quant), aggressive (more quant, lower cost).
[05:54] Diego Alvarez: Also factor in prefix caching; if you have high reuse we can reduce GPU needs.
[05:59] Nadia Ortiz: We have a lot of repeated routes at peak, maybe 30% reuse.
[06:03] Diego Alvarez: That will help costs a lot. We'll include cache assumptions in the model.
[06:07] Asha Kaur: Any blockers we should surface now?
[06:10] Ben Lowe: Firewall approvals and KMS policy gating from security. Also we need an internal compliance review for the vendor; Maya said you'd send the SOC docs.
[06:19] Maya Chen: Yup, I'll push the compliance pack after the call.
[06:23] [06:23] Priya Rao: Quick note about SSO—do you use SAML? We'll need SSO to map RBAC for admin roles.
[06:29] Asha Kaur: Yes SAML via Okta. We'll provide metadata.
[06:33] Maya Chen: Great, we'll add SSO onboarding step.
[06:36] Ravi Patel: Anything else on runbook? We prefer a 24-hr warm standby for the first two weeks post go-live.
[06:43] Priya Rao: We can do that—CS will coordinate.
[06:46] Diego Alvarez: One final technical note—if you plan to run very long sequence lengths occasionally (like 3-4k tokens), call that out. Memory planning will shift.
[06:56] Nadia Ortiz: We do have some outliers for large customer manifests, up to 3.5k tokens.
[07:02] Diego Alvarez: Noted—we'll include outlier handling and spool fallback to a smaller model for those cases.
[07:09] Maya Chen: Ok, let's recap next steps quickly.
[07:13] Maya Chen: Action items: Redwood send sizing & pricing (Maya), SE send benchmark harness (Diego), CS draft runbook (Priya). Westlane share VPC info and SOC contacts (Asha/Ravi). Schedule pilot start 2028-02-27.
[07:28] Asha Kaur: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:31] Ravi Patel: Appreciate the clarity, looking forward to the worksheet.
[07:34] Ben Lowe: Thanks all.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Thanks team, we'll follow up with an email and the docs. Bye.

End of transcript. Note: transcript contains occasional mis-attribution and imperfect auto-transcription (names, acronyms).
